page: Amazon Web Services vt1.6xlarge is a specialized accelerated computing instance designed for video transcoding and media pipeline processing. It features 24 vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity totals 48.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB per core. The defining capability of this instance is the inclusion of two Xilinx U30 media accelerator cards carrying a combined total of 48 GB of VRAM. Networking operates with a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, and no local ephemeral storage is bundled.

Benchmark results reflect the instance's reliance on second-generation Intel Xeon scalable architecture. The CPU delivers average multi-core output, indicated by a PassMark CPU score of 20,589.93, a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,518.0, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 19,941.29. Single-threaded metrics show lower relative capability, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the bottom 10% (1,008.78) and single-threaded gzip compression categorized as weak at 22.62 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth reaches 110.18 GB/sec uncached, with write throughput measured at 48.66 GB/sec.

Because the vt1.6xlarge pairs custom Xilinx ASIC-based accelerators with a modest 2:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, its hardware design prioritizes video encoding and transcode throughput rather than general server computing. Tasks requiring intense general-purpose single-core execution or large in-memory footprints face performance constraints. Workloads involving live streaming, media transcoding pipelines, and video processing that directly utilize the Xilinx U30 hardware units represent the primary operational targets.
description: Amazon Web Services vt1.6xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built for video transcoding pipelines. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor providing 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores at 2.5 GHz, paired with 48.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. Acceleration is provided by two integrated Xilinx U30 media processing cards offering 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance includes a 6 Gbps baseline network interface and provides no local storage. Benchmark figures place multi-core compute and memory metrics in the middle 50% tier, while single-core processing ranks lower. Because resources are architected around ASIC video acceleration rather than heavy general-purpose CPU compute, this instance is primarily fitted for live video broadcasting, transcoding, and streaming services.
